title: Punishment of the Rebels (Punishment of the Sons of Korah)

image.credit: Photograph via Wikimedia Commons (Botticcelli, Sandro - The Punishment of Korah and the Stoning of Moses and Aaron - 1481-82.jpg)

source.label: Wikipedia: his only significant time away from Florence included “the Sistine Chapel in Rome in 1481–82”
Wikipedia: Botticelli was summoned “to fresco the walls of the newly completed Sistine Chapel”
Wikipedia: it “tells of a rebellion by the Israelites against Moses and Aaron”
Wikipedia (Florentine painting): “Some of the best known painters of the earlier Florentine School are Fra Angelico, Botticelli…”

work.text: Botticelli differs from his colleagues in imposing a more insistent triptych-like composition, dividing each of his scenes into a main central group with two flanking groups at the sides, showing different incidents.

The Punishment of the Sons of Corah contains what was for Botticelli an unusually close, if not exact, copy of a classical work. This is the rendering in the centre of the north side of the Arch of Constantine in Rome

moment.text: In 1481, Pope Sixtus IV summoned Botticelli and other prominent Florentine and Umbrian artists to fresco the walls of the newly completed Sistine Chapel. … The Florentine contribution is thought to be part of a peace deal between Lorenzo Medici and the papacy.
The theme of the decoration was a parallel between the lives of Moses and Christ, as a sign of continuity between the Old and the New Testament.

matters.text: he received from the Pope a good sum of money, the whole of which he consumed and squandered in a moment during his residence in Rome, where he lived in haphazard fashion, as was his wont.

matters.lead: Vasari’s version of the Roman months:

matters.text: On 17 February 1482 his contract was renewed, including the other scenes to complete the chapel's decoration. However, on the 20th of the same month, his father died: he returned to Florence, where he remained.
